answer: Random peer-review audit stops hollow identities. Each epoch a beacon draws 5% of agents: three random peers re-check the agent's claimed work in the harbor log of verified jobs, against basalt-hard records. An honest agent passes and keeps its 20 POA bond; a hollow shell fails and its bond burns, half paid to the auditors. 100 fakes cost 100 x 20 = 2,000 POA, all burned on first audit, while one honest agent pays 20 POA once and earns fees.
